facts.text: The 2.0 feature list advertises a Gym-compatible environment implementation
The single-agent environment class is Env, a gymnasium.Env subclass
Env.__init__ requires a Config and builds a SimulatorRunner and a task config manager from it
Env accepts only env_num 1 and at most one robot per episode
The action space is a hardcoded Dict with the key move_along_path, a Sequence of Tuples of three Box(-inf, inf) entries, independent of the Config
The observation space is a hardcoded Dict with position Box shape (3,) and orientation Box shape (4,), all bounds -inf to inf, independent of the Config
Env.reset accepts seed and options but uses neither; it delegates to runner.reset and returns the robot observation plus info['task_config']
Env.step wraps the action as {robot_name: action}, calls runner.step, and returns observation, reward, terminated, False and info; truncated is always False
When the runner reports reward -1, Env.step reports 0.0; every other reward is reported unchanged
A step before the first reset returns an empty observation, 0.0, False, False and None
SimulatorRunner.setup_isaacsim imports isaacsim.SimulationApp and constructs it
The only Simulator member is ISAACSIM = 'isaac_sim'
SimConfig defaults physics_dt and rendering_dt to 1/60 s
The prerequisites list NVIDIA Omniverse Isaac Sim 4.5.0 and an NVIDIA GPU of RTX 2070 or higher
The vectorized internutopia.core.vec_env.Env documents itself as NOT gymnasium compatible

determinism.notes: no determinism claim is made: Env.reset accepts a seed but never uses it (gym_env.py:62-87), and Isaac Sim was not run or measured. The fake backend is deterministic for a fixed command sequence but is not presented as a replay claim about the upstream simulator.

gaps: the gate's model is a pure-Python kinematic stand-in: no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction or physics engine
the fake sets the pose from the supplied path points directly; no actuator, controller, sensor, camera or noise model is represented

the fake receives the action-space object directly and interprets move_along_path itself; upstream Env.step wraps the action as {robot_name: action} and the runner dispatches it to the configured controllers (gym_env.py:130-131), and no controller or robot model is present here

the fake's observation is the hardcoded observation_space shape (position, orientation), while upstream returns the robot observation mapping produced by the runner (gym_env.py:84-85 and 136-137); the configured robot's observations are not represented
no Isaac Sim run was made: the upstream environment needs Isaac Sim 4.5.0 and an NVIDIA GPU (README.md:69-71), and the fake was not compared with it
the upstream Env.reset accepts seed and options but uses neither, so no seeded replay claim is made and Isaac Sim determinism was not measured
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0; one tick advances the fake by one step only, and timestep_ms is the SimConfig physics_dt default (config/__init__.py:21), not a measured interval of the fake
snapshot and restore are not offered: Env exposes no get_state/set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
